title: Tuskegee football and Benjamin Stevenson
summary: Wilson remembers the undefeated Tuskegee football teams and the runner Benjamin Stevenson, compared locally to Red Grange.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Another thing comes to mind about Tuskegee that might be of interest to some people -- Tuskegee was quite a school sports, especially football. The baseball was not outstanding, but the Tuskegee football team went for, oh, five years undefeated. I remember one period there in the twenties, largely due to a man named Benjamin Stevenson, his name was. They called him Steve, which was his nickname, and he was one of the most marvelous football players of the day, and of course, the local people like to compare him with the outstanding white football player of Notre Dame, Red Grange -- he's a big name, at least, but down in Tuskegee, Steve could run as good as Red Grange, and it was very common for Benjamin Stevenson to run from kickoff to touchdown -- that was a very usual occurrence for this man.
And he was a marvelous player -- I remember him.
We had no publicity in those days, too.
No, that's right. But oh, Stevenson --
it took more than two men to tackle Stevenson. Fabulous football player.
